bus.name: turn.started
bus.description: Published once per turn when memory takes the user's message as turn `turn` (`TurnMemory.persistMessage`; `Agent.turn` runs it before the host's `use`). `runId` names the run, `userMessage` is what the user said. Not journaled from the bus: the session stored its own `turn.started` when the turn began. A subscription made in `use` never sees it; one in the host's per-turn layer or a session plugin does.

stored.where: the session's own `turn.started`, written when the turn began

schema.description: Published once per turn when memory takes the user's message as turn `turn` (`TurnMemory.persistMessage`; `Agent.turn` runs it before the host's `use`). `runId` names the run, `userMessage` is what the user said. Not journaled from the bus: the session stored its own `turn.started` when the turn began. A subscription made in `use` never sees it; one in the host's per-turn layer or a session plugin does.

bus.name: step.started
bus.description: Published by the step loop as each step starts. `planned` is true for step 0 of a host-planned batch, which makes no provider call; `activeTools` are the tool names the step offers the model. Journaled as `step.started`.

schema.description: Published by the step loop as each step starts. `planned` is true for step 0 of a host-planned batch, which makes no provider call; `activeTools` are the tool names the step offers the model. Journaled as `step.started`.

bus.name: tool.started
bus.description: Published by the tool registry just before a tool's handler runs. `invocationId` (`<runId>:call:<n>`) pairs it with its `tool.completed`; `input` is the decoded parameters; `labels` and `stage` come from the tool's annotations. A refused call (inactive, forbidden, denied, over a limit) publishes no `tool.*` event; `step.ended.results` lists every recorded result. Journaled as `tool.started`, input included.

schema.description: Published by the tool registry just before a tool's handler runs. `invocationId` (`<runId>:call:<n>`) pairs it with its `tool.completed`; `input` is the decoded parameters; `labels` and `stage` come from the tool's annotations. A refused call (inactive, forbidden, denied, over a limit) publishes no `tool.*` event; `step.ended.results` lists every recorded result. Journaled as `tool.started`, input included.

bus.name: tool.progress
bus.description: Published by `publishToolProgress` from inside a tool handler, between that call's `tool.started` and `tool.completed` (same `step`, `invocationId` and `tool`). `channel` is stdout or stderr for a command's output as it arrives, status for anything else the tool reports; `text` is that output or message. Transient: never journaled; `tool.completed` carries the result.

schema.description: Published by `publishToolProgress` from inside a tool handler, between that call's `tool.started` and `tool.completed` (same `step`, `invocationId` and `tool`). `channel` is stdout or stderr for a command's output as it arrives, status for anything else the tool reports; `text` is that output or message. Transient: never journaled; `tool.completed` carries the result.

bus.name: tool.completed
bus.description: Published by the tool registry when a handler returned or failed (`ok`). `result` is the decoded value, `encoded` its wire form as the model receives it. `durationMs` runs from just after `tool.started` to the handler's exit, so it includes any wait for the tool's read or write lane. Journaled as `tool.completed` without `input`, `result` and `encoded`: memory keeps the call and its result (`memory.message`, `memory.tool-result`).

schema.description: Published by the tool registry when a handler returned or failed (`ok`). `result` is the decoded value, `encoded` its wire form as the model receives it. `durationMs` runs from just after `tool.started` to the handler's exit, so it includes any wait for the tool's read or write lane. Journaled as `tool.completed` without `input`, `result` and `encoded`: memory keeps the call and its result (`memory.message`, `memory.tool-result`).

bus.name: step.ended
bus.description: Published by the step loop after the step's tail is recorded. `status` is completed, failed or cancelled; `results` are the step's recorded tool results (memory entry, tool call id, tool, ok), in log order, refused calls included. Journaled as `step.ended`.

schema.description: Published by the step loop after the step's tail is recorded. `status` is completed, failed or cancelled; `results` are the step's recorded tool results (memory entry, tool call id, tool, ok), in log order, refused calls included. Journaled as `step.ended`.

bus.name: completion.evaluated
bus.description: Published by the step loop after `step.ended`, with the verdict of the host's completion policy for that step. A verdict that awaits tasks is evaluated again once they finish, publishing a second event. Journaled as `completion.evaluated`.

schema.description: Published by the step loop after `step.ended`, with the verdict of the host's completion policy for that step. A verdict that awaits tasks is evaluated again once they finish, publishing a second event. Journaled as `completion.evaluated`.

bus.name: skills.activated
bus.description: Published by the tool registry when skills (and their tools) become active: always-on skills, the intent matcher, the model's `load_skill`, or the host. Not journaled from the bus: memory records the activation as `memory.skills`.

schema.description: Published by the tool registry when skills (and their tools) become active: always-on skills, the intent matcher, the model's `load_skill`, or the host. Not journaled from the bus: memory records the activation as `memory.skills`.

bus.name: context.built
bus.description: Published before each provider call, once the step's context is built (none for a planned step 0). It carries the memory strategy and its version, the context and system-prompt fingerprints, the token estimate and reservation, how many compactions the build applied, and the active tools. Journaled as `context.built`; the full request is journaled beside it as `request.prepared`.

schema.description: Published before each provider call, once the step's context is built (none for a planned step 0). Journaled as `context.built`; the full request is journaled beside it as `request.prepared`.

bus.name: decision.recorded
bus.description: Published by `recordDecision`, for example when `turn.tools.select` or `apply` records the skill selection: the decision record holds the candidates, the policy version and what was chosen. Journaled as `decision.recorded`.

bus.name: assistant.message
bus.description: Published by the step loop once per provider response, after that step's tools ran and its tail is recorded: the text, the reasoning, the model, the tool calls and the token usage (input with its cache reads and writes inside, output with its reasoning inside). A host-planned step 0 carries zero usage. Journaled only as `step.usage` (step, model, usage): the content itself is memory's `memory.message`.

fields.name: usage
fields.type: { inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, reasoningTokens }

schema.description: Published by the step loop once per provider response, after that step's tools ran and its tail is recorded: the text, the reasoning, the model, the tool calls and the token usage (input with its cache reads and writes inside, output with its reasoning inside). A host-planned step 0 carries zero usage. Journaled only as `step.usage` (step, model, usage): the content itself is memory's `memory.message`.

bus.name: assistant.delta
bus.description: Published by the step loop for each streamed increment while `limits.streaming` is on (the default), on channel text, reasoning or tool-params; `id` groups the increments of one content part. Transient: never journaled, and restated in full by `assistant.message`. A stream that falls back to a non-streamed call publishes none.

bus.name: turn.ended
bus.description: Published once when the turn's reply is recorded (`TurnMemory.persistReply`, from `guardTurn`), also when the turn fails, with outcome failed; `usage` is the turn's usage, the usage of its `assistant.message` events summed (`RunContext.usage`). Under `Agent.turn` it is published after `use`, the host's per-turn layer and the turn-dependent plugins have closed, and their subscriptions with them: only a subscription whose scope is still open sees it, such as one made with `Scope.provide(observerScope)` over the caller's outer scope, or one registered around `TurnLive` by a host composing the turn itself. Otherwise read the `TurnResult` `Agent.turn` returns (its `usage` is the same total), or the stored `turn.reply` and `turn.ended`, and `turnUsageOf` over the stored events. Not journaled from the bus: memory stores `turn.reply` and the session its own `turn.ended` (reason and failure, no usage).

fields.name: usage
fields.type: { inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, reasoningTokens }

The key was begun before with another message or command.
An inbox turn found nothing to take (inbox turns only).

beginCodes.http: 429 for a quota or rate, 403 when not allowed

No such session for this owner.

The turn's scope closed before the turn was ended (reason failed or interrupted).
The turn's holder stopped writing and another instance reaped it (reason interrupted).
An inbox turn run by `Sessions.drain` failed.
Memory was asked to record, or for the turn's number, before the user's message was taken.
The user's message was taken twice in one turn.
Memory numbered the user's message differently from the turn the session stored.
The host event's name is one of the reserved kinds.
Reactions nested deeper than `maxEventDepth` (8 by default).
A background handler died with a defect; the turn fails when the bus drains.
The payload did not encode with the host event's schema.
A service the turn needs is not provided by the agent's plugins or the turn's services.
The plugin graph cannot be built (a missing provider, a cycle, a misplaced turn-dependent plugin).
A plugin's options did not decode with its schema.
